span.label: A DIAGNOSTIC CATEGORY BEING BUILT: 4,785 CANDIDATE DEFINITIONS OF ONE DISORDER, ENUMERATED AND SCORED - prolonged grief disorder, proposed for DSM-V and ICD-11, whose symptom list and threshold are FITTED to data rather than agreed by a vote or counted across a literature
span.quote: A total of 291 bereaved respondents were interviewed three times, grouped as 0–6, 6–12, and 12–24 mo post-loss. Item response theory (IRT) analyses derived the most informative, unbiased PGD symptoms. Combinatoric analyses identified the most sensitive and specific PGD algorithm that was then tested to evaluate its psychometric validity.

span.label: which grief symptoms are informative and unbiased enough to define a disorder, and which combination of them - how many, of which set, after how long - best separates cases from non-cases
span.quote: In Phase 1 of the analysis, the aim was to limit the set of candidate symptoms for PGD to those that were informative and unbiased. In Phase 2 of the analysis, the goal was to construct an objective, reliable, valid symptom criterion standard for PGD by which to evaluate alternative diagnostic algorithms for meeting symptom criteria for PGD. The aim of Phase 3 of the analysis was to identify a specific, optimum diagnostic algorithm for meeting symptom criteria for PGD among a large set of candidate algorithms.

span.label: a six-phase psychometric procedure that reduces 22 candidate symptoms to 12, builds a criterion standard for `caseness` where none existed, enumerates 4,785 candidate algorithms and selects one - yearning plus at least five of nine symptoms, at least six months after the death, with functional impairment
span.quote: A total of 4,785 of these algorithms for meeting the symptom criterion for PGD were enumerated [i.e., the sum of (11 choose n ×( n −3) for n = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, where (11 choose n ) represents the number of ways of choosing n of 11 nonmandatory symptoms, n ∈ {5, 6, 7, 8, 9}, and ( n −3) represents the number of values of k ∈ {3, …, n −1}, considered for a given value of n ] and subsequently evaluated with respect to the criterion standard. Algorithms requiring yearning and as few as three of five, and as many as eight of nine, additional symptoms were considered.

span.label: grief that does not remit - distinguishable from uncomplicated grief and from depression in course, treatment response and outcome, and excluded from both diagnostic manuals on the grounds that it is an expectable response
span.quote: Nevertheless, the DSM-IV excludes grief as a disorder on the grounds that it is “an expectable and culturally sanctioned response to a particular event” [12] .

span.label: **A FIFTH PROCEDURE FOR A CONTESTED TERM - OPTIMISE**: `Item response theory (IRT) analyses derived the most informative, unbiased PGD symptoms. COMBINATORIC ANALYSES IDENTIFIED THE MOST SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC PGD ALGORITHM that was then tested to evaluate its psychometric validity.` The corpus holds definitions COUNTED (sarcopenia's 138), VOTED (three consensus panels), REFUSED (five experts who decline to converge) and SYNTHESISED. **This one is FITTED** - the symptom set and the threshold are the output of a search, not of an agreement
span.quote: A total of 291 bereaved respondents were interviewed three times, grouped as 0–6, 6–12, and 12–24 mo post-loss. Item response theory (IRT) analyses derived the most informative, unbiased PGD symptoms. Combinatoric analyses identified the most sensitive and specific PGD algorithm that was then tested to evaluate its psychometric validity.

span.label: **AND THE SEARCH SPACE IS PRINTED**: `A TOTAL OF 4,785 OF THESE ALGORITHMS for meeting the symptom criterion for PGD WERE ENUMERATED [i.e., the sum of (11 choose n x( n -3) for n = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 ...] and subsequently evaluated with respect to the criterion standard. Algorithms requiring yearning and AS FEW AS THREE OF FIVE, AND AS MANY AS EIGHT OF NINE, additional symptoms were considered.` **4,785 definitions of one disorder, all of them defensible, one of them selected** - and the paper gives the formula, so the count is checkable
span.quote: A total of 4,785 of these algorithms for meeting the symptom criterion for PGD were enumerated [i.e., the sum of (11 choose n ×( n −3) for n = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, where (11 choose n ) represents the number of ways of choosing n of 11 nonmandatory symptoms, n ∈ {5, 6, 7, 8, 9}, and ( n −3) represents the number of values of k ∈ {3, …, n −1}, considered for a given value of n ] and subsequently evaluated with respect to the criterion standard. Algorithms requiring yearning and as few as three of five, and as many as eight of nine, additional symptoms were considered.

span.label: **AND THE RULER IS BUILT FROM THE SAME TWELVE ITEMS IT MEASURES**: `IN THE ABSENCE OF AN ESTABLISHED, STANDARD METHOD FOR DIAGNOSING PGD, THERE WAS A NEED TO DEVELOP A CRITERION STANDARD for `caseness` of PGD by which the performance of alternative algorithms for PGD could be evaluated.` The standard is `Scores from a 2-PL IRM for PG BASED ON THE 12 INFORMATIVE, UNBIASED SYMPTOMS`, cut at the point where `AGREEMENT BETWEEN RATER AND MINIMUM-THRESHOLD PG ATTRIBUTE ASSESSMENTS ... WAS MAXIMIZED`. **The algorithm then scores sensitivity 1.00 and specificity 0.99 against it.** Those two numbers measure how well a subset of twelve items reproduces a threshold fitted to all twelve
span.quote: It was decided that a criterion standard for caseness should be informed by clinical judgment, but should also be a function of PG symptom severity. Dichotomized IRM PG attribute scores, informed by rater assessments of PGD, would provide objective, reliable, valid criterion standard diagnoses for PGD. Scores from a 2-PL IRM for PG based on the 12 informative, unbiased symptoms were used to order individuals in terms of PG symptom severity. Agreement between rater and minimum-threshold PG attribute assessments of caseness of PGD was maximized to establish an optimum minimum threshold for caseness of PGD along this IRM scale.

span.label: AND THE JUDGEMENT THE STANDARD IS CALIBRATED TO IS THE ONE THE PAPER CALLS UNRELIABLE: `rater assessments of PGD WERE SUBJECTIVE, WERE MADE WITHOUT EXPLICIT REFERENCE TO ANY ESTABLISHED CRITERIA, and were not always consistent with more objective, reliable assessments of PG ... (i.e., RATERS ASSIGN PGD TO SOME INDIVIDUALS WITH LOW SCORES, AND NOT TO OTHERS WITH HIGH SCORES, on the PG attribute scale).` The cutoff is then chosen to agree with those same raters as far as possible - `greatest agreement (kappa = 0.68)`. **A standard that is neither the clinical judgement nor independent of it**
span.quote: As a potential criterion standard for PGD, the rater determination of caseness of PGD had the advantage of reflecting experienced clinical judgment. However, rater assessments of PGD were subjective, were made without explicit reference to any established criteria, and were not always consistent with more objective, reliable assessments of PG as measured with IRM scores for the underlying PG attribute (i.e., raters assign PGD to some individuals with low scores, and not to others with high scores, on the PG attribute scale).

span.label: **AND MEMBERSHIP IS DECIDED BY THRESHOLDS ALL THE WAY DOWN**: a symptom is PRESENT `IF RATED 4 OR 5, AND ABSENT IF RATED 1, 2, OR 3, on its five-point scale`; a symptom is ADMISSIBLE if its peak information is at least 20% of the most informative symptom AND it shows no differential item functioning; a person is a CASE at `YEARNING AND AT LEAST FIVE OF THE NINE` symptoms, `AT LEAST SIX MO FROM THE DEATH`. **Four nested cuts, three of them chosen by the analysts**, and the five-point severity scale disappears into a yes/no at the very first one
span.quote: Based on prior work [23] , [59] , a symptom was considered present if rated 4 or 5, and absent if rated 1, 2, or 3, on its five-point scale.

span.label: **AND FOUR SYMPTOMS WERE EXPELLED FROM THE DISORDER FOR BEHAVING DIFFERENTLY IN DIFFERENT PEOPLE**: `A TOTAL OF FOUR OF 16 INFORMATIVE SYMPTOMS WERE FOUND TO BE BIASED WITH RESPECT TO TIME FROM LOSS, GENDER, AND/OR RELATIONSHIP TO THE DECEASED.` Six more had already gone for carrying too little information. 22 candidates -> 16 informative -> 12 unbiased -> **9 in the published criteria**. `Loneliness as a result of the death`, present in 57.1% of this sample, is dropped on all three bias grounds at once. **A diagnostic concept trimmed to what is measurement-invariant** - the criterion is psychometric, not clinical
span.quote: DIF analysis of between-group differences in item location parameters was used to evaluate potential biases in the assessment of the remaining 16 informative, candidate symptoms for PGD with respect to age (less than 65 y versus greater than or equal to 65 y), gender (male versus female), education (beyond versus not beyond high school), relationship to the deceased (spouse versus nonspouse), and time from loss (0–6 versus 6–12 mo post-loss). Figure 2 displays item characteristic curves by group, spouse, and nonspouse, for two items eliminated from consideration as possible symptoms for assessing and diagnosing PGD due to evidence of DIF using a 16-item 2-PL IRM. A total of four of 16 informative symptoms were found to be biased with respect to time from loss, gender, and/or relationship to the deceased.

span.label: AND ONE SYMPTOM WAS MADE COMPULSORY BY TWO DIFFERENT AUTHORITIES AT ONCE: `BASED ON CONSENSUS OPINION of the previously mentioned expert panel [23] , AND CONFIRMED BY RESULTS showing yearning was the most common (68.3%) and most informative ( I max = 0.94) of the 12 items ..., YEARNING WAS SPECIFIED AS A MANDATORY SYMPTOM.` A vote and a statistic agreeing about the same item, and the paper says which came first
span.quote: Based on consensus opinion of the previously mentioned expert panel [23] , and confirmed by results showing yearning was the most common (68.3%) and most informative ( I max = 0.94) of the 12 items and provided the maximum information and the lowest degree of severity (Θ max = −0.53), yearning was specified as a mandatory symptom.

span.label: AND THE SIX-MONTH THRESHOLD HAS AN EVIDENTIAL WARRANT, WHICH MOST DURATION CRITERIA DO NOT: `the ACUTE temporal specification WAS NOT SIGNIFICANTLY ASSOCIATED WITH ANY OF THE EXAMINED OUTCOMES ... These results indicate that DIAGNOSES OF PGD BEFORE 6 MO POST-LOSS DO NOT EFFECTIVELY IDENTIFY bereaved individuals at risk of long-term dysfunction, WHEREAS DELAYED AND PERSISTENT TEMPORAL SUBTYPES DO.` The waiting period is not a convention - it is the point at which the diagnosis starts predicting. **A null result used constructively, to place a boundary**
span.quote: In Table 2 , we see that the acute temporal specification was not significantly associated with any of the examined outcomes evaluated 12–24 mo post-loss. Delayed was significantly ( p <0.001) associated with suicidal ideation and poor quality of life. Persistent was significantly ( p <0.01) associated with mental disorders (MDD, PTSD, or GAD), suicidal ideation, and poor quality of life. Delayed or persistent was significantly ( p <0.05) associated with psychiatric disorders (MDD, PTSD, or GAD), suicidal ideation, functional disability, and poor quality of life. These results indicate that diagnoses of PGD before 6 mo post-loss do not effectively identify bereaved individuals at risk of long-term dysfunction, whereas delayed and persistent temporal subtypes do.

span.label: AND CAUSATION IS WRITTEN INTO THE MEMBERSHIP TEST: `E. Impairment : THE DISTURBANCE CAUSES CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT IMPAIRMENT in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning`, added `TO BE CONSERVATIVE IN OUR DIAGNOSIS`. **The causal clause is not a finding about the disorder; it is a condition for being counted as having it** - and it was added, along with the timing rule, to hold down false positives rather than because the data demanded it
span.quote: To reduce further the likelihood of a false-positive diagnosis, a timing criterion (Criterion D) was added to specify that a diagnosis not be made until at least 6 mo have elapsed since the death. This would exclude the acute cases described above in which a person with initially high levels of grief in the first few months experiences declines in grief intensity at and beyond 6 mo post-loss. To be conservative in our diagnosis of PGD, we also added a requirement that the symptomatic distress be associated with functional impairment (Criterion E).

span.label: AND THE DISORDER IS DEFINED PARTLY BY WHAT IT IS NOT: `F. Relation to other mental disorders : THE DISTURBANCE IS NOT BETTER ACCOUNTED FOR BY MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER, OR POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER.` The positive evidence for the boundary is elsewhere - `discriminant validity ... (Phi with MDD = 0.36; PTSD = 0.31; GAD = 0.17)` - but the criterion itself is a **precedence rule between categories**, not a property of the patient
span.quote: D. Timing : Diagnosis should not be made until at least six months have elapsed since the death. E. Impairment : The disturbance causes clinically significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning (e.g., domestic responsibilities). F. Relation to other mental disorders : The disturbance is not better accounted for by major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, or posttraumatic stress disorder.

span.label: **THE PAPER AND ITS OWN EDITORS DISAGREE ABOUT THE DOMAIN OF VALIDITY, IN THE SAME RECORD**. The authors: `a distinct advantage of IRT is that IT PRODUCES GENERALIZABLE RESULTS REGARDLESS OF SAMPLE CHARACTERISTICS ... THE RESULTS ARE EXPECTED TO BE GENERALIZABLE TO MOST BEREAVED INDIVIDUALS.` The PLoS Medicine Editors' Summary, printed above it: `BECAUSE MOST OF THE STUDY PARTICIPANTS WERE ELDERLY WOMEN WHO HAD LOST THEIR HUSBAND, FURTHER VALIDATION IS NEEDED to check that these symptoms and algorithm ALSO APPLY TO OTHER TYPES OF BEREAVED PEOPLE such as individuals who have lost a child.` polman2011 printed its validity domain twice and agreed with itself; **this record prints two incompatible answers, in the voices of the authors and the journal**
span.quote: In addition, the symptoms retained were only those proven to be invariant across gender, time from loss, and kinship groups (e.g., IRT DIF analysis removed items that performed differently based on whether or not the deceased was a spouse) and a distinct advantage of IRT is that it produces generalizable results regardless of sample characteristics [66] . Thus, the results are expected to be generalizable to most bereaved individuals.

span.label: AND HERE IS THE OTHER HALF OF THAT DISAGREEMENT, IN THE JOURNAL'S OWN VOICE: `These findings validate a set of symptoms and a diagnostic algorithm for PGD. BECAUSE MOST OF THE STUDY PARTICIPANTS WERE ELDERLY WOMEN WHO HAD LOST THEIR HUSBAND, FURTHER VALIDATION IS NEEDED to check that these symptoms and algorithm ALSO APPLY TO OTHER TYPES OF BEREAVED PEOPLE SUCH AS INDIVIDUALS WHO HAVE LOST A CHILD.` The Editors' Summary is written by PLoS Medicine, not by the authors, and it is part of the record: **a limitation stated by the publisher over the authors' stated position**
span.quote: These findings validate a set of symptoms and a diagnostic algorithm for PGD. Because most of the study participants were elderly women who had lost their husband, further validation is needed to check that these symptoms and algorithm also apply to other types of bereaved people such as individuals who have lost a child.

span.label: AND THE GENERALISATION ARGUMENT IS THE EXCLUSION ARGUMENT RUN BACKWARDS: the symptoms `WERE ONLY THOSE PROVEN TO BE INVARIANT ACROSS GENDER, TIME FROM LOSS, AND KINSHIP GROUPS (e.g., IRT DIF ANALYSIS REMOVED ITEMS THAT PERFORMED DIFFERENTLY based on whether or not the deceased was a spouse)`. **Removing the items that varied is offered as the reason the result will not vary.** It is a real argument, and it protects only against variation in the ITEMS THAT SURVIVED, in the four grouping variables that were tested, in this sample
span.quote: In addition, the symptoms retained were only those proven to be invariant across gender, time from loss, and kinship groups (e.g., IRT DIF analysis removed items that performed differently based on whether or not the deceased was a spouse) and a distinct advantage of IRT is that it produces generalizable results regardless of sample characteristics [66] . Thus, the results are expected to be generalizable to most bereaved individuals.

span.label: AND THE SAMPLE SELECTED AGAINST THE CASES THE INSTRUMENT IS FOR: `Of the 575 potential participants contacted, 317 (55.1%) AGREED TO PARTICIPATE`, and of those who declined, `BEING ... TOO UPSET ( n = 27; 10.5%)`. The authors draw the conclusion themselves - `the prevalence rate of PGD reported here MAY BE AN UNDERESTIMATE` - in `A RESILIENT COMMUNITY SAMPLE in which rates of mental illness were lower than ... other bereavement studies (e.g., 9% FOR MDD COMPARED WITH 22% IN THE FIRST YEAR OF WIDOWHOOD)`. **The people too distressed to be interviewed are the people the diagnosis is for**
span.quote: Study participants may have been less distressed than study nonparticipants. Given the relatively low rates of MDD in the YBS sample and that 10.5% refused participation in the YBS due to being “too upset,” the prevalence rate of PGD reported here may be an underestimate.

span.label: AND THE REFUSAL FIGURES ARE PRINTED, WHICH IS WHY THAT IS SAYABLE AT ALL: `Of the 575 potential participants contacted, 317 (55.1%) AGREED TO PARTICIPATE. Reasons for nonparticipation included ... BEING TOO BUSY ( n = 46; 17.8%) OR TOO UPSET ( n = 27; 10.5%) ... NONPARTICIPANTS WERE MORE LIKELY TO BE MALE (37.2% versus 25.9%) AND OLDER.` **A 45% refusal rate, itemised by reason** - and the two reasons that correlate with the condition under study are the two the authors then reason from
span.quote: Of the 575 potential participants contacted, 317 (55.1%) agreed to participate. Reasons for nonparticipation included reluctance to participate in research ( n = 11; 4.3%); being too busy ( n = 46; 17.8%) or too upset ( n = 27; 10.5%); “doing fine” ( n = 23; 8.9%); “not interested” or “no reason” ( n = 145; 56.2%); and “other” reasons ( n = 6; 2.3%). Nonparticipants were more likely to be male (37.2% versus 25.9%, p <0.001) and older (mean age = 68.8 y versus 61.7 y, p <0.001) than participants.

span.label: AND THE SAMPLE IS DEFENDED BY DECLARING IT THE PROTOTYPE: `we consider WIDOWHOOD FOLLOWING AN OLDER SPOUSE'S DEATH FROM NATURAL CAUSES TO BE THE PROTOTYPICAL CASE OF BEREAVEMENT. In the US, 84% OF ALL DEATHS occur among individuals who are 65 y and over ..., and LESS THAN 7% OF DEATHS ARE FROM UNNATURAL CAUSES.` A base-rate argument for a category's central case - **and the criteria that come out of it are then proposed for every bereaved person in two international classifications**
span.quote: Although there is a need to confirm the results in nonwidowed bereaved persons, we consider widowhood following an older spouse's death from natural causes to be the prototypical case of bereavement. In the US, 84% of all deaths occur among individuals who are 65 y and over [71] , and less than 7% of deaths are from unnatural causes (e.g., unintentional injuries, assault, suicide) [72] . Given that in later life one's spouse/partner is the person most likely to be adversely affected by the death, a sample of older widowed persons surviving the death of a spouse from natural causes provides an important sample in which to develop and test criteria for a bereavement-related mental disorder.

span.label: AND THE CONCLUSION'S FUNDING CLAIM AND THE FOOTNOTE ARE ABOUT DIFFERENT THINGS: `it is noteworthy that THIS STUDY WAS FEDERALLY FUNDED BY THE US NIMH, and NO PART OF THIS RESEARCH WAS SPONSORED BY PRODUCERS of a potential therapeutic remedy for PGD` sits in the same record as `MBF RECEIVED CONSULTANT FEES over the past 5 years FROM ROCHE, CORCEPT, WYETH, CEPHALON, ASTRA-ZENECA, SHIRE, GSK, AND ELI LILLY for preparing diagnostic interviews`. Both are true and they are not in contradiction - **one is about the study's sponsorship, the other about an author's income** - and a reader who takes the first as covering the second is reading a scope that is not there
span.quote: In light of the recent concerns about financial conflicts of interest in psychiatric research, especially that which involves pharmaceutical manufacturers, it is noteworthy that this study was federally funded by the US NIMH, and no part of this research was sponsored by producers of a potential therapeutic remedy for PGD.

span.label: AND THE FOOTNOTE ITSELF, VERBATIM, SO THE SCOPE IS VISIBLE: `MBF RECEIVED CONSULTANT FEES OVER THE PAST 5 YEARS FROM ROCHE, CORCEPT, WYETH, CEPHALON, ASTRA-ZENECA, SHIRE, GSK, AND ELI LILLY FOR PREPARING DIAGNOSTIC INTERVIEWS AND/OR CONDUCTING DIAGNOSTIC TRAININGS at investigator meetings.` Disclosed as required, on the record, and **it is disclosure of a kind the conclusion's sentence does not cover** - the conclusion speaks about who paid for the study
span.quote: MBF received consultant fees over the past 5 years from Roche, Corcept, Wyeth, Cephalon, Astra-Zeneca, Shire, GSK, and Eli Lilly for preparing diagnostic interviews and/or conducting diagnostic trainings at investigator meetings.

span.label: an inter-rater agreement gate on the interviewers - `nearly perfect agreement (kappa >= 0.90)` with the investigators across five pilot interviews before being allowed to collect data
span.note: eliminates: measurement noise in the very judgements the criterion standard is later calibrated against · outcome: held
span.quote: Interviewers were required to demonstrate nearly perfect agreement (κ≥0.90) with the YBS investigators for diagnoses of psychiatric disorders (e.g., MDD) and PGD in five pilot interviews before being permitted to interview for the study.

span.label: testing the proposed criteria in the subsample with no concurrent MDD, PTSD or GAD ( n = 215)
span.note: eliminates: the objection that PGD's predictive power is depression's or PTSD's, wearing a new name · outcome: held
span.quote: Our results indicate that PGD meets DSM criteria for inclusion as a distinct mental disorder on the grounds that it is a clinically significant form of psychological distress associated with substantial disability. Findings from this field trial of consensus criteria for PGD confirm prior work demonstrating the distinctiveness of the symptoms of PGD (e.g., [15] , [18] – [20] , [22] , [26] , [27] , [29] – [31] ). The proposed diagnostic algorithm for PGD has quite incomplete overlap with established mental disorders commonly occurring among recently bereaved individuals (MDD, PTSD). Further, our results indicate that in the absence of mental disorders found in DSM-IV (e.g., MDD), the proposed algorithm for PGD predicts substantial dysfunction—impairment missed by the current psychiatric diagnostic system.

span.quote: Studies have shown that symptoms denoting complicated, or prolonged, grief are distinguishable from symptoms of uncomplicated grief [15] – [18] and that only the former are associated with significant impairment [15] – [25] .

span.quote: The course and response to treatment of PGD differ from those of normal grief [48] , [49] and depression [48] – [52] . Tricyclic antidepressants alone and with interpersonal psychotherapy have proven ineffective relative to placebo for the reduction of PGD symptoms [50] – [52] . By contrast, randomized, controlled trials of psychotherapy designed specifically for PGD have demonstrated efficacy for PGD symptom reduction [53] , [54] .

span.label: bereavement
span.quote: In the DSM-IV , bereavement is classified as a “V” code; that is, an “other condition that may be a focus of clinical attention” [12] . Similarly, in the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision ( ICD-10 ) [13] , bereavement is classified as a “Z” code, which refers to “occasions when circumstances other than a disease or injury result in an encounter or are recorded by providers as problems or factors that influence care” [14] .

span.label: Symptoms of PGD
span.quote: Symptoms of PGD were assessed with the rater version of the Inventory of Complicated Grief—Revised (ICG-R) [34] – [36] , [40] , [41] , [45] , [59] , a structured interview designed to assess a wide variety of potential PGD symptoms, using five-point scales to represent increasing levels of symptom severity. The ICG-R is a modification of the Inventory of Complicated Grief (ICG) [15] that includes all the symptoms proposed by the consensus panel [23] and additional symptoms enabling the testing of alternative diagnostic algorithms [22] . The ICG-R and the original ICG have both proven highly reliable (e.g., [15] , [25] , [36] , [41] ) (e.g., Cronbach's α>0.90; test-retest reliability coefficient = 0.80 [15] ) and to possess criterion validity [15] , [21] , [24] , [25] , [45] .
